programme: NR0B1 (DAX1) is the anchor of a hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal/gonadal steroidogenic transcriptional module: it targets the SF1 partner NR5A1 plus the steroidogenic enzyme/receptor battery STAR, CYP11A1, CYP17A1 and MC2R. DLX3 reaches the same pathway through the steroidogenic enzyme HSD3B1. NFYC targets the mineralocorticoid receptor NR3C2 and its effector channel SCNN1A. FOXD2 reaches the cAMP-PKA arm (PRKAR1A), the adrenergic receptor ADRA1B, the androgen receptor AR, and the PCC/PGL susceptibility gene NF1. HESX1 and CREB3L1 sit upstream at pituitary/hypothalamic level, driving gonadotropin genes (GNRH1, LHB, PROP1) and neurohypophyseal hormones (AVP, OXT) respectively. Together these six factors sketch a steroid-hormone biosynthesis-and-signaling axis running hypothalamus to pituitary to adrenal/gonadal steroidogenesis.
role_in_a: Chronic HPA-axis hypofunction, blunted cortisol/ACTH coupling, and altered gonadotropin/neurohypophyseal (AVP, OXT) signaling are long-standing candidate contributors to fibromyalgia's pain amplification, fatigue and hormone-linked symptom fluctuation; this module is plausible transcriptional machinery for that dysregulation if it operates in FM tissue.
role_in_b: Pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma are neuroendocrine tumors of the adrenal medulla or extra-adrenal paraganglia. NF1 (a FOXD2 target) is one of their established germline drivers, and the adjacent adrenal cortex steroidogenic machinery (STAR, CYP11A1, CYP17A1, HSD3B1, MC2R, NR5A1, NR3C2) can be co-perturbed with the chromaffin-cell compartment these tumors arise from.
shared_axis: If transcriptional control of this hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal/gonadal steroidogenic module is disturbed in both conditions, it would link a tumor that grows within the adrenal gland (PCC/PGL) to a chronic pain syndrome long hypothesized to involve HPA-axis and neuroendocrine dysregulation (fibromyalgia) — the same regulatory axis operating in two different failure modes, structural/neoplastic versus functional/dysregulated.
reasoning: The six factors form a coherent, textbook steroidogenic/neuroendocrine axis, not an arbitrary grab-bag, so this clears the coherence bar. But Open Targets records no association for any of the twelve concordant factors in either disease, and the only paper retrieved for the whole set (TRIM28, PMID 40338225) concerns HERV activation, a mechanism unrelated to this module and to TRIM28 not even being one of the carrying factors. PCC/PGL are chromaffin-cell catecholamine tumors, not adrenocortical steroidogenic tumors, so the fit to disease B is anatomical proximity rather than cell-type match; the fit to disease A rests entirely on the general HPA-axis-in-fibromyalgia hypothesis, which this record does not evidence. Only 2 independent cohort pairs underlie the 40 comparisons, a thin base for the recurrence counts.
support: PMID 40338225 — shows TRIM28/HERV activation distinguishes fibromyalgia from ME/CFS, but TRIM28 is not part of this steroidogenic module and the paper does not bear on NR0B1, DLX3, NFYC, FOXD2, HESX1, CREB3L1 or on Pheochromocytoma_and_Paraganglioma; none found for the carrying factors in either disease.
how_to_falsify: Test whether NR0B1, DLX3, NFYC, FOXD2, HESX1 and CREB3L1 (or their targets STAR, CYP11A1, CYP17A1, HSD3B1, NR3C2, AVP, OXT, GNRH1) are differentially expressed or bound (ChIP-seq/ATAC) in PCC/PGL tumor tissue versus normal adrenal medulla and cortex, and separately whether fibromyalgia patients show altered expression of this same factor set or altered HPA/HPG hormone dynamics (cortisol, ACTH, gonadotropins) tracking with symptom severity. If neither disease shows coordinated perturbation of this specific factor set beyond generic adrenal or blood expression, the account is wrong.
caveats: Tissue pairing is the coarse label adrenal|blood: the steroidogenic targets recovered (STAR, CYP11A1, CYP17A1, HSD3B1, NR3C2, MC2R) are adrenal cortex genes, while PCC/PGL arise from medullary chromaffin cells or extra-adrenal paraganglia, so the anatomical match is looser than the tissue label implies. Only 2 independent cohort pairs underlie the 40 patient-group comparisons, so the recurrence counts are not 40 independent replications. CREB3L1 shows 0/10 targets confirmed by ReMap binding (SOX11, excluded from this account, similarly shows only 1/11) — these are network-inferred edges, not ChIP-confirmed. The single-view exclusions (BRCA1, IRF4, ESR2, TBX21, RFX3, etc.) rule out DNA-damage-response and generic-immune framings as one-cohort artifacts; the tissue-generic exclusions (PRDM1, STAT3, IRF1, GFI1, E2F1-3, ETS2, CREB5, LITAF, BRCA1) rule out a generic immune/proliferation master-regulator story as the explanation for either disease's involvement.
